title: Handle chimeric MS2 spectra
doc: Finds the other ions co-isolated in the precursor window of each MS2 spectrum, writes the purity of the precursor and the intruders, and leaves the spectrum as it is: the scores that read it discount the peaks an intruder can explain. Nothing is removed from the spectrum.

features.title: Aligned feature table, the whole one and not a filtered view (for the intruders)

algorithms.title: Purity flag
algorithms.doc: Share of the MS1 signal in the isolation window that belongs to the precursor (within 5 ppm, PURITY_PPM), taken in the MS1 scans before and after the MS2 scan; the spectrum is kept and flagged (fill_purity in crates/mzlab-feat/src/interp/ms2link.rs).

purity_min.title: Purity below which a spectrum is chimeric
purity_min.description: A spectrum whose purity is lower is flagged CHIMERIC=true (the same limit as tp.link); PURITY_BAND is low under 0.5, medium up to this limit and high above

algorithms.title: Intruder features
algorithms.doc: Lists the features of the same polarity inside the isolation window and within the RT distance, the nearest in m/z first, so that the fragments they explain can be discounted (ms2_engine/chimeric.rs). Evidence for the chemist: no level changes.

window.title: Isolation window
window.description: Absent: the instrument of the campaign decides, 3.0 for a Fusion and 1.5 for the others (default_window); a feature is co-isolated within half of it

rt_tol.title: RT distance
rt_tol.description: Features of the same polarity farther apart in RT are not co-isolated

algorithms.title: MS1 isolation window
algorithms.doc: Reads the raw MS1 scan of the precursor and lists the ions of the window that are neither the precursor nor its M+1 and M+2 (ms1_metrics in crates/mzlab-feat/src/attributio/review/raw.rs).

chim_rel.title: Co-isolated ion
chim_rel.description: An ion of the MS1 isolation window this large against the precursor peak is listed as co-isolated

chim_cap.title: Cap of a proposal
chim_cap.description: A co-isolated ion this large caps the proposal of the review (propose.rs); the level stays the chemist's

algorithms.title: Library-assisted deconvolution
algorithms.doc: Explains the spectrum as a non-negative mix of the library spectra whose precursor lies in its isolation window and writes the share of each and the share left unexplained; the spectrum stays as it is (ms2_engine/deconv.rs).

references.note: library-assisted deconvolution of chimeric MS2 spectra

applicability.note: Data-dependent MS2 with wide windows and a library that covers the intruders

window.title: Isolation window
window.description: Absent: the instrument of the campaign decides (default_window); library spectra whose precursor lies within half of it are candidates

tol_da.title: Fragment tolerance
tol_da.description: A library peak explains a peak of the spectrum within this distance

min_share.title: Smallest share listed
min_share.description: A library spectrum that explains less of the spectrum than this is not listed

title: Formula from MS1
doc: Candidate molecular formulas of each feature from the exact mass and, when the isotope finder finds a pattern, from the isotope pattern. The list is ordered by score and by a confidence that is a share of the list, never an identification: the chosen formula is the chemist's.

z.title: Charge
z.description: Absent: the isotope finder decides, and 1 when it finds no pattern; above 1 the formulas are those of the ion itself

elements.title: Elements
elements.description: Ranges as C:0-50,H:0-100. Absent: C:0-50,H:0-100,N:0-8,O:0-15,P:0-2,S:0-3 plus the heavy elements the finder sees in the spectrum; the text given is searched as written

max_charge.title: Highest charge tried
max_charge.description: Charges the isotope finder looks at

require_c13.title: Require 13C peak
require_c13.description: The isotope finder accepts a pattern only with the 13C peak

algorithms.title: Mass and isotope pattern
algorithms.doc: Exact-mass search over the element ranges (compose in crates/mzlab-core/src/composition.rs), scored on the mass error and on the fit of the isotope pattern that the finder takes from the spectrum (untargeted/formula_id.rs). Without a pattern only the mass term counts.

references.note: heuristic rules that filter molecular formulas of accurate mass (RDB, nitrogen rule, element ratios)

title: Formula from MS2
doc: Assigns to each cleaned peak the closest sub-formula of the ion of the candidate formula and gives the neutral losses. A sub-formula supports the FORMULA, never the structure: isomers share it.

formulas.title: Formulas with the peaks they explain

ppm_ion.title: Precursor tolerance
ppm_ion.description: Precursor against the ion of the formula, the adduct with the smallest error of the polarity

ppm_frag.title: Fragment tolerance
ppm_frag.description: Fragment against a sub-formula of the ion (the MS2 tolerance of SIRIUS)

max_subformulas.title: Sub-formula limit
max_subformulas.description: Above this many sub-formulas the table is not built

algorithms.title: Sub-formulas
algorithms.doc: Closest sub-formula of the ion within ppm_frag (RDBE at least -0.5; a Na or K adduct keeps its cation in every fragment). The same peaks shifted by 20, 35 and 50 mDa in both directions are assigned again: the share explained by chance (decoy) is reported (review/explain.rs).

algorithms.title: Hydrogen rearrangements
algorithms.doc: A peak that no sub-formula explains is tried again shifted by +1, -1, +2 and -2 hydrogens, the fragment taking those hydrogens. Score = sum of intensity * (1 - 0.25 * |shift|) over the sum of intensities (attribute in ms2_engine/rearrange.rs). The penalty and the score are our choice, not those of MS-FINDER.

references.note: hydrogen rearrangements between the two sides of a bond break

title: Compare MS2 spectra
doc: Scores each query MS2 spectrum against a spectral library inside the precursor window and keeps the best candidates per feature. A candidate is a hit with its scores and shared peaks, never an identity: the level is decided by annot.level.

tol_da.title: Fragment tolerance
tol_da.description: Fragment matching between spectra, the GNPS convention

tol_ppm.title: Fragment tolerance (ppm)
tol_ppm.description: Above 0 it replaces tol_da: a peak pairs within this many ppm of its own m/z (high-resolution spectra); the analogue search keeps tol_da

precursor_ppm.title: Precursor tolerance
precursor_ppm.description: Library precursor against the precursor of the feature

precursor_da.title: Precursor window (low resolution)
precursor_da.description: Above 0 the precursor window is this many Da either side instead of precursor_ppm, for unit-resolution data (use a fragment tolerance of 0.3 to 0.5 Da); 0 keeps the ppm window

name_contains.title: Library name contains
name_contains.description: Only library entries whose name contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. The spectra still decide the score

rt_tol.title: RT tolerance
rt_tol.description: Above 0, a library entry whose retention time differs from the RT of the query spectrum by more than this is not a candidate; entries or queries without a retention time are kept. The candidate carries rt_delta_min (query minus library) when both are known; 0 switches the filter off. Not used by the tree algorithm

adduct_contains.title: Library adduct contains
adduct_contains.description: Only library entries whose adduct (for example [M+H]+) contains this text (any case) are candidates; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

instrument_contains.title: Library instrument contains
instrument_contains.description: Only library entries whose instrument or instrument type contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example Orbitrap or QTOF; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

ce_contains.title: Library collision energy contains
ce_contains.description: Only library entries whose collision energy text contains this text (any case) are candidates, for example 30 or HCD; empty keeps all. Not used by the tree algorithm

decoys.title: Decoys
decoys.description: spectrum: a decoy spectrum (random fragments, same intensities) is searched beside every library entry and each best hit carries decoy_q, the q-value of the batch; it is a lower bound of the true error rate (isomers and analogues are not random errors). Works with the entropy, cosine and modified cosine scores (not tree; the q-value counts the candidates inside the precursor window; an .mzlib is read back to spectra and rebuilt with the decoys); none leaves the hits as they are

matched_peaks.title: Matched peaks
matched_peaks.description: On: every candidate also lists matched_peaks, the pairs of peaks behind its score (m/z and relative intensity of the query and of the library spectrum, and whether the precursor shift was needed), so the match can be checked peak by peak; the scores do not change. Not used by the tree algorithm

score_terms.title: Score terms
score_terms.description: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as a weighted sum of named terms (the contribution of each matched pair, the rest in one term) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

algorithms.title: Spectral entropy
algorithms.doc: Entropy similarity of the merged spectrum after the cleaning of ms_entropy (entropy_from_pairs in crates/mzlab-lib/src/scores.rs); the search of ms2_engine/matcher.rs.

references.note: entropy similarity and its intensity weighting

min_score.title: Minimum score
min_score.description: A hit below this entropy similarity is dropped

min_shared.title: Minimum shared ions
min_shared.description: Matched ions between query and library spectrum; two peaks can score high on a sparse spectrum

algorithms.title: Cosine
algorithms.doc: One-to-one peak pairs within the tolerance, the highest intensity product first (cosine_from_pairs in crates/mzlab-lib/src/scores.rs); the review reads it with the GNPS preparation (gnps_cosine).

algorithms.title: Modified cosine
algorithms.doc: Peaks may also pair at the precursor difference, for analogues that differ by one modification (modified_cosine in crates/mzlab-lib/src/scores.rs).

references.note: modified cosine: peaks matched directly or shifted by the precursor mass difference

applicability.note: Analogues and transformation products of a known parent

analog_window_da.title: Analogue window
analog_window_da.description: Library precursors within this distance of the feature are candidate analogues

analog_prefilter.title: Candidates scored
analog_prefilter.description: Candidates that pass the prefilter and are scored with the modified cosine

analog_min_shift_da.title: Smallest shift
analog_min_shift_da.description: A smaller precursor difference is the same ion, not an analogue

exact_ppm.title: Exact match
exact_ppm.description: A precursor difference within this is an exact match, not an analogue

delta_formula_mda.title: Delta formula
delta_formula_mda.description: Free search of a CHNOPS formula for the precursor difference

algorithms.title: MSn tree
algorithms.doc: Compares an unknown MSn graph with the entries of an MSn library whose precursor is inside the window; the MS2 entropy, the tree and the shared losses stay apart as three scores with their proofs (msngrafo/cerca.rs). The output is msncerca/1 or, with tree_output, candidates/1: nothing is called a match.

applicability.note: The query port takes the msngrafo/1 graph and the library port an msnlib/1 file declared as a library; precursor_ppm (or precursor_da), tol_da and top_n are the windows and the cut of the search; name_contains keeps the entries whose id or private name has the text. decoys do not apply

min_prove.title: Minimum shared peaks
min_prove.description: A candidate needs this many peaks shared with the unknown in its best MS2 pair

tree_output.title: Output
tree_output.description: msncerca: the msncerca/1 text of msn-lib search. candidates: the candidates/1 of the other algorithms (score = MS2 entropy similarity; the tree and loss scores and the proofs in the tree block), which annot.level reads

title: In silico fragmentation
doc: Breaks each candidate structure of a local list bond by bond and ranks it by the weight of the peaks its fragments explain. The result is a hypothesis with its proofs (peaks explained, mass error), never an identity. No network: the list is read from the campaign folder.

candidates.title: Structures ranked by the fragments they explain

db_ppm.title: Mass tolerance
db_ppm.description: Candidates within this of the neutral mass of the precursor

max_bonds.title: Bonds broken
max_bonds.description: A candidate is broken bond by bond up to this many bonds

score_terms.title: Score terms
score_terms.description: On: every candidate also carries score_terms, its score as the share of each explained peak and the key of its formula in the Theory; the scores themselves do not change

algorithms.title: Bond-wise fragmenter
algorithms.doc: Score = sum of mz^0.421 * intensity^0.1307 of the explained peaks over the sum of all the peaks (fragmenter_score in ms2_engine/insilico.rs). Not MetFrag: no bond-energy term and no 0.005 Da + 10 ppm tolerance.

references.note: bond-wise in silico fragmentation of candidate structures
weights of the explained peaks (mass 0.421, intensity 0.1307)

title: Retention time plausibility
doc: Compares the retention time of a candidate with what the campaign's own confident identifications predict. A warning aid that ranks or doubts a candidate: it never applies a level and does not tell isomers apart.

standards.title: Identified features of the campaign with their RT

algorithms.title: RT against logP
algorithms.doc: Calibrates RT against the logP of the Level 1 and robust Level 2a features of one polarity, one logP source per fit, at least 15 calibrants (MIN_N), and checks a candidate against the window (calibrate and check in crates/mzlab-feat/src/attributio/review/rtlogp.rs).

rt_logp_k.title: Window width
rt_logp_k.description: Prediction window = plus or minus this many times the residual MAD

lc_dwell_min.title: Gradient delay
lc_dwell_min.description: Dwell volume over flow; the gradient itself ([[t, %B], ...]) is read from the campaign

rt_logp_terms.title: Score terms
rt_logp_terms.description: On: the check also writes its residual as a sum of named terms (observed value, intercept, one term per descriptor) and the key of its formula in the Theory; the residual itself does not change

algorithms.title: Random forest
algorithms.doc: Random forest of regression trees on a Morgan-type fingerprint with our own hash (not the bits of RDKit), trained on the standards of the campaign (RtModel in ms2_engine/rtpredict.rs).

references.note: regression forest: bootstrap samples, random split search
circular (Morgan) fingerprint of the structure graph

applicability.note: At least 10 standards whose structure is read; the model follows the column and gradient of the campaign

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Seed of the bootstrap; 100 trees over a 2048-bit fingerprint of radius 2 (N_TREES, N_BITS)

title: Identification level
doc: Gives each feature the level its evidence reaches (1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, 4, 5; 0 = detected, not annotated), with the basis and the reasons. Level 2b is never given by the program: the chemist decides it. A CANOPUS class gives no level: it is a separate annotation.

references.note: the five-level scale of identification confidence

candidates.title: Library, in silico and suspect candidates

annot.title: Chosen annotation with its level and evidence

spec_sim_min.title: Library cosine
spec_sim_min.description: Cosine of a library match, every spectral-library source

spec_peaks_min.title: Shared fragments
spec_peaks_min.description: Shared fragment ions of a library match, every library (SIRIUS, GNPS2, mzMine)

library_conflict.title: Conflicting libraries
library_conflict.description: best_match: the libraries are one library; level3: sources naming different structures give Level 3

library_conflict_margin.title: Conflict margin
library_conflict_margin.description: The best match keeps Level 2a only if its cosine exceeds the best match of a different structure by this much

cosmic_min.title: COSMIC confidence
cosmic_min.description: Confidence of the Level 3 gate; 0.64 is the threshold of the COSMIC paper, roughly an FDR of 10 %, a practical guide and no guarantee

canopus_min.title: Class probability
canopus_min.description: A CANOPUS class is shown, as an annotation of its own that gives no level, at or above this probability

rt_group_tol_min.title: RT group
rt_group_tol_min.description: Features of one identity farther apart in RT (consecutive) are different peaks

putative_library_level3.title: Putative library entries
putative_library_level3.description: Library entries named Spectral Match to ... (propagated annotations) are taken to Level 3

algorithms.title: Cascade of the sources
algorithms.doc: Reference standard, spectral library, CSI:FingerID with COSMIC, formula, mass, in this order of basis (basis_level in crates/mzlab-feat/src/attributio/annotate/settings.rs; gates in gates.rs, reasons in reasons.rs).

references.note: COSMIC confidence score and its 0.64 threshold

applicability.note: A level needs MS2 or a standard; at unit resolution the ceiling is Level 4

title: Regulatory lists
doc: Compares the identities (and the suspects) with versioned snapshots of regulatory and priority lists. A list entry says what a compound is on a list, nothing about this sample; the snapshots are read from the campaign folder with their hash, no network.

window.title: Mass window
window.description: Entries of the lists outside this range of monoisotopic mass are left out; absent: all the entries

algorithms.title: List membership
algorithms.doc: B1: the identities against the entries of the lists by whole InChIKey; a match on the first block only is flagged as such (match_campaign in crates/mzlab-feat/src/attributio/reglists/b1.rs).

algorithms.title: Suspect screening
algorithms.doc: B2: the list entries as suspects by exact mass (5 ppm over [M+H]+, [M+NH4]+, [M+Na]+, [M-H]- and [M+Cl]-), classes A-D and X, and a robust line of RT against logP (2.5 SD) when the registry has XLogP3 (screen_campaign in reglists/screen.rs).

algorithms.title: MS2 confirmation
algorithms.doc: B3: a suspect of class A, B or C is Level 2a with a SIRIUS or MetFrag cosine of at least 0.70 on 6 peaks, Level 3 with a COSMIC confidence of at least 0.64, otherwise rejected or unconfirmed; the chemist's decisions win (evaluate in reglists/confirm.rs).

title: Aquatic hazard
doc: One acute and one chronic aquatic hazard category per chemical identity, from versioned snapshots read from the campaign folder with their hash, no network. A hazard class is a property of a structure, not a risk: no concentration, no PNEC. A Level 3 identity carries the caveat of its candidate structure.

annot.title: Rows with the aquatic hazard record

algorithms.title: Tiers T1 to T5
algorithms.doc: The first tier with a category wins, acute and chronic separately: T1 regulatory (CLP harmonised, curated), T2 measured (ECOTOX), T3 notified (PubChem GHS H-statements), T4 predicted (curated judgement, then ECOSAR 2.2), T5 not assessable. Degradability is unknown for almost every compound, so every chronic category assumes not rapidly degradable and says so (record in crates/mzlab-feat/src/attributio/tox/hazard.rs).
